currentBehavior.finding: RLS predicates and groups already live in core metadata, extend SyncableEntity, and participate in application manifests and universal identifiers.

Record shares already use one cross-object workspace table. Identity includes objectMetadataId, recordId, principalId, rowCause and sourceId. Principals are EVERYONE, WORKSPACE_MEMBER or ROLE; access levels NONE, READ, READ_WRITE, FULL. Causes OWNER, MANUAL, RULE, APPLICATION. Generic user-defined share-rule configuration was not found; RULE is used by workflow-run grant producers.

Named shares can bypass the role object gate and RLS for SELECT and UPDATE when sharingReach=WORKSPACE and IS_RECORD_LEVEL_SHARING_ENABLED. ROLE_ACCESS preserves the role ceiling. General everyone shares cannot widen beyond the role. Fields are checked separately. FULL share holders still need role UPDATE to manage sharing.

RLS currently compiles at query time and supports current-member field substitution, including custom member fields. Applicable roles intersect (user/application/agent scopes), rather than representing multiple additive human roles. Mutations validate before and after values, refusing updates that leave the RLS update policy.

Existing inherited readability declares relation-field universal identifiers on objects, supports many-to-one, one-to-many and morph siblings, recursively compiles parent policies at read time, with max depth 3. Parent alternatives and own shares are ORed. Notes/tasks have special detached behavior and deleted-link timing for trash. This is not a reusable explicit path-definition UI/model yet.

Repository before-execute policy applies to root and joined aliases. Search uses that repository. Event delivery uses an in-memory evaluator of the shared policy tree across subscriptions, webhooks, workflows, agents and logic functions. All must remain consistent when adding materialized reads; not only GraphQL lists.

Transaction event callbacks run after commit in process; errors are logged and swallowed. WorkspaceEventEmitter uses EventEmitter2.emit. Share storage disables event emission explicitly. No durable permission propagation outbox/reconciliation system was found.

RLS service enforces EnterprisePlanService.isValid AND BillingEntitlementKey.RLS. Current FeatureFlagKey has record-level-sharing flag, but no RLS rollout flag. No separate sharing billing entitlement check was found in inspected sharing service; many underlying sharing files bear Enterprise license headers, which must be preserved.

Record exports use CommonFindManyQueryRunnerService with workspace auth. File downloads use signed workspace/file JWTs in FileByIdGuard, not a fresh record authorization check; already-issued URLs are a separate revocation scope. FilesField token expiry is checked and private cache max-age is 86400 seconds.

materializationInvestigation.roleModel: RoleTarget unique per workspace/userWorkspace, many targets share the same role; viewer field values are bound in build-row-level-permission-record-filter at query time today
dependencyChangesToCover: time passing for any time-relative predicates if supported
materializationInvestigation.candidateToEvaluate: Role-wide role arrays plus viewer-dependent materialized access identifiers; consider grouping identical role+parameter bindings to avoid duplicating per-user grants. No implementation chosen.
materializationInvestigation.recommendation: Prefer compact per-action permission/access identifiers: role-wide entries plus internal scopes tied to role, rule/version and bound current-member values. Resolve active scope membership per auth context; never union user and application authority into one bypass. A per-member-only array is simple but expands broad rules by member count. Scope grouping compresses owner/region examples but cannot bound all arbitrary high-cardinality predicates; benchmark those. New scope bindings may need backfill. This is a recommendation, not an approved final schema.

findings: Dense city case examines only 97 company candidates and 97 permission probes to return 50 rows.

sharingStorageRecommendation.status: Updated for user-selected query routing; previous direct-share OR collection path superseded
sharingStorageRecommendation.sourceGrants: One cross-object recordShare table in the workspace schema; approximately50K source grants. Keep target identity, recipient, action set, source identity and audit information.
sharingStorageRecommendation.directReadPath: Live source queries for sharing and point operations. Collections use record action arrays containing eligible direct-sharing effects as well as inherited/RLS access.
sharingStorageRecommendation.inherited: Live declared-path evaluation for point/sharing operations; materialized access on business records for collections. No persistent per-descendant recordShare rows.
sharingStorageRecommendation.automaticRules: A new criteria-based automatic-sharing editor and generic rule-definition table are out of scope (question 19). Preserve existing application/workflow-produced source grants and their source identities in workspace recordShare storage.
sharingStorageRecommendation.inheritanceDefinitions: Portable metadata field paths, at most3hops.
sharingStorageRecommendation.revocation: Recompute from remaining direct/parent/rule sources, preserving overlapping grants. Capture old relationship endpoints transactionally; use bounded recomputation or conservative rebuild when old reachability cannot be recovered.
sharingStorageRecommendation.groupIdentity: Source-grant identity and access-group identity are distinct. Recipient membership groups can be reused across grants; do not blindly remove a shared group when one source is revoked.
sharingStorageRecommendation.provenance: On-demand indexed source/path explanations initially; add a derived provenance index only if measured workloads justify its potentially large cardinality and maintenance cost.

queryRoutingDecision.projectionCoverage: Complete eligible record access including direct shares, inherited shares and RLS. The former direct-share OR lookup on collection reads is superseded.
queryRoutingDecision.commonSemantics: One policy definition compiled for live evaluation and materialization; same Receive, record capabilities, field restrictions, max-three-hop paths, authority intersection and active revision.
queryRoutingDecision.freshness: Live routes use authoritative source state, including ancestor inputs, in a coherent snapshot; no stale parent permission arrays or silent projection fallback. Primary/fenced reads and version-validated policy/member/role caches required.
queryRoutingDecision.consistency: Accepted propagation delay remains on collections: selected record fields may still be returned after live access is revoked; new live access can precede collection visibility. No per-row live post-filtering of collection pages.
queryRoutingDecision.routing: Declared query scope, not output length. A filtered LIMIT1 query remains a collection; nested collections use projections even under a live detail root.
queryRoutingDecision.mutationRecommendation: Use live transactional authorization for point edits/deletes and existing post-update checks. Bulk operations may select candidates through projections then validate live actions in bounded SQL batches. These are proposed engineering extensions, not separately confirmed product answers.

engineeringDecisions.receiveAndInheritance: Receive admits source shares on the original target. A declared inheritance path carries the granting parent's effective actions, capped by the final target capabilities and field restrictions; absence of a separate target Receive grant does not veto inheritance. Relation-only intermediaries are not extra granting parents.
engineeringDecisions.creation: Preserve separate create and proposed-value authorization; no parent-conditioned creation editor and no implicit permanent creator grant.
engineeringDecisions.mutations: Use live transactional action validation for point mutations and bounded SQL batches for bulk targets; retain the deferred post-update restriction.
engineeringDecisions.publicationFence: Shared transaction-scoped workspace fence for permission-relevant source/projection writers, exclusive for short publication check/switch after catch-up; release and retry if pending work remains. Audit all writers and validate concurrency before relying on this design.
